title: Mapping telescope of an exhaustive module-complex filtration
statement: For a commutative ring R, a cochain complex L of R-modules, complexes F_n, monomorphisms i_n:F_n→L and maps s_n:F_n→F_{n+1} with s_n followed by i_{n+1} equal to i_n, suppose every element in every degree of L comes from some F_n. In the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] there is an object S and a colimit cofan exhibiting S as the coproduct of the Q(F_n), indexed by ULift ℕ in the module universe, and maps making S→S→Q(L)→S[1] a distinguished triangle.

proof.text: Index the complex coproduct by ULift ℕ from the outset. Define a on its n-th summand as the coprojection minus step n followed by the next coprojection, and define b as the sum of the inclusions into L. Coproduct extensionality and compatibility prove a followed by b is zero.

The fully proved private helper telescope_injective computes the zero-th and successor components of a on finitely supported tuples. If a x is zero, induction on the component number shows every component of x is zero. The fully proved private helper telescope_kernel passes to the quotient by the image of a. A single component can be moved to any later stage without changing its quotient class or its image in L. Induction on finitely supported tuples, moving the two terms to the maximum of their stages, represents any class by one component. A tuple in the kernel of b therefore has a representative whose inclusion into L is zero; injectivity of that inclusion kills it, proving membership in the image of a.

The fully proved private helper filtration_telescope_shortExact identifies the evaluated categorical coproduct with the concrete direct sum using their colimit universal properties. It identifies the evaluated maps a and b with the linear maps used by telescope_injective and telescope_kernel. Evaluation preserves monomorphisms, so each inclusion is injective. Exhaustiveness supplies a preimage of every element under b. Thus every degree is short exact; HomologicalComplex.shortExact_of_degreewise_shortExact proves the complex sequence short exact.

Apply DerivedCategory.triangleOfSESδ and DerivedCategory.triangleOfSES_distinguished [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] to the short exact sequence. Use derivedModuleDirectSums [lem-pc-derived-module-direct-sums] directly with the index ULift ℕ to exhibit Q of the complex coproduct as the required derived coproduct. These are the object S, its coprojections j, and the three arrows in the conclusion; no separate reindexing is needed.

proof_origin.place: Remark 09PB (remark-P-resolution), displayed telescope triangle; the omitted degreewise algebra is expanded by the worker and fully proved in Lean using private helpers.
